statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON (green). Tail is low at 11% while Stress is extreme at 82%.
recommendation: Tail remains well below the 25% block threshold, so the deterministic mapping resolves to EA_ON for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. NQ trades at 29,398.75, down 0.17%, in a fifth consecutive hour inside a 29,359.25-29,508.25 band. The 29,359.25 low is a marginal new extreme made in the last hour, but it was bought back roughly 40 points rather than extended, and the 29,508.25 high has not been retested since it was rejected four hours ago. Both extremes have therefore produced retracements, which is mean-reverting behaviour rather than the persistent directional efficiency that defines a tail path. Stress stays extreme on Brent above $100, a 10-year at 4.86% and roughly even odds of a September rate increase. A narrow danger window is published around the 12:30 UTC producer price release and the 13:30 UTC US cash open, where the published conditional Tail reaches the watch band.
headline: NQ holds 29,398.75 in a fifth hour inside 29,359.25-29,508.25 after a marginal new low was bought back, with VIX flat at 16.50 while Brent at $101.92 and a 4.86% 10-year keep Stress extreme into the 12:30 UTC producer price release
body:
Observed evidence at the assessment cutoff: Nasdaq-100 E-mini futures print 29,398.75, down 50.00 points or 0.17% against a 29,448.75 prior settle, inside a session range of 29,359.25 to 29,508.25 after opening at 29,458.50. That 149-point band is roughly 0.51% wide and has now contained price for a fifth consecutive hour. In the last hour the low was extended marginally, by under five points, to 29,359.25 and price has since recovered about 40 points from it, so the new extreme produced a retracement rather than repeated extension. The 29,508.25 high was set four hours ago, rejected immediately and never retested. Both extremes have therefore been faded, and the intervening path is a slow drift within the band rather than a directional run. The Nasdaq-100 cash index closed the 9 September session at 29,421.55, down 86.15 points or 0.29%, within a 29,334.40 to 29,563.60 range and beneath a 29,507.70 prior close.

Cross-asset conditions remain restrictive, with the energy leg easing slightly at the margin. Brent trades at $101.92, up 0.71%, having eased from $102.18 an hour earlier, and WTI is $97.28, up 1.28%. The driver remains the continuing exchange of strikes between US and Iranian forces around the Strait of Hormuz alongside reported attacks on Saudi energy facilities, a supply-risk channel rather than a demand story. The US 10-year yield is 4.86%, up 1.8 basis points and the highest since 2023, while the 2-year is 4.45%, up 0.3 basis points; the curve is steepening modestly with the 30-year at 5.31%, which is a term-premium move rather than a policy repricing. VIX is 16.50, up 0.24%, inside a 16.29 to 16.59 range, so options are not pricing a tail event. Delayed cross-asset context shows Nasdaq futures lagging both S&P 500 and Dow futures, all seven tracked semiconductor names lower on the latest session with a mean change of -0.78%, and mixed megacaps with Apple firm and Nvidia slightly lower. That is relative weakness in the index's own leadership without a broad defensive rotation impulse, which supports a mixed dominant mode.

The scheduled path is the reason Stress is extreme rather than the price path. Producer prices, core producer prices and weekly jobless claims are all scheduled for 12:30 UTC, roughly two hours after the cutoff, with existing home sales at 14:00 UTC and the consumer price release the following midday. Market-implied odds of a September rate increase have been reported near a coin flip since the Jackson Hole address, so an inflation print that confirms energy pass-through is a live yield catalyst. None of that has printed at the cutoff, and no outcome is assumed here. Following the calibration that event importance and forecast dispersion inform Stress and Confidence rather than Tail, the current Tail is scored on the observed two-sided band at 11%, one point above the prior assessment to reflect the marginal new low and the mild downward drift. The published danger window is deliberately narrow, spanning the release and the US cash open, where conditional Tail reaches 20% and 22% without approaching the 25% block threshold.

lookbackSummary: Across the 24 hours to 09:00 UTC the mapped policy state was EA_ON in 22 of the 23 available slots, with one WATCH hour at 12:00 UTC on 9 September when Tail reached 20% during a trend-down European session. Tail ranged from 8% to 20% and has held a tight 8-11% band for the last eighteen hours as retracements continued to appear at both ends of the range. Stress climbed from 79% to a sustained 80-83% as Brent broke $100 and the 10-year set successive cycle highs, and has stayed at 80-82% overnight. Confidence held between 87% and 89% throughout. The 10:00 UTC slot on 9 September has no published assessment and is marked unavailable.
outlookSummary: The published conditional path holds Tail at 11-12% through the remaining European session, lifts it to 20% in the 12:00 UTC release hour and a horizon peak of 22% in the 13:00 UTC hour where post-release repricing would overlap the US cash open, then decays it to 13-19% across the US afternoon with a 15% power-hour step and to a 9-13% band overnight into the European session that precedes the consumer price release. Only the 12:00 and 13:00 UTC slots map to WATCH; no slot reaches the 25% block threshold on current evidence. Stress stays in the extreme band for most of the horizon because Brent above $100, a 10-year at its highest since 2023 and roughly even odds of a September rate increase are regime features that a single release does not clear, easing to the high band only during the quiet overnight hours. Confidence decays from 88% to 60% across the horizon as slots move further beyond the observed sample. Every slot beyond the current clock hour is conditional and describes checkpoints and invalidations rather than observed structure.
